correctness.rationale: The nonproportional linear factors and conic Hessian determinant -6 give the distinct reduced components over C. Independent exact calculation of all cross products and memberships gave six line-double points (four on the conic) and five line-triple points (two on the conic), exhausting the 21 line pairs. The restrictions of q to the seven line equations have discriminants 4,4,4,1,1,1,1 in the coordinate bases used for replay, so intersections with q are transverse on every line. The shared points exhaust the 14 line–conic Bézout incidences, leaving only two ordinary nodes, seven ordinary triple points and two ordinary quadruple points. For local multiplicity d=2,3,4 the leading homogeneous product h of distinct tangents has gradient a homogeneous regular sequence of degree d-1. Its Jacobian quotient vanishes above degree 2d-4, so all terms of order d+1 or more lie in the square of the maximal ideal times J(h). The sufficient analytic right-determinacy criterion makes h d-determined, and the local Tjurina numbers are (d-1)^2 in this specific range (ordinariness alone would not justify a blanket statement for every multiplicity). The two frozen quartic triples were independently substituted into the integer polynomial gradient and their determinant with the Euler row expanded, giving exactly 0,0,-243F. Saito's criterion gives the free logarithmic basis over C; since the Euler derivation sends F to 9F and the quartic triples annihilate F, the latter are an AR(F) basis. The free-curve identity (9-1)^2-4*4=48 also checks the same global Tjurina number. All equations have rational coefficients.
residual_risks: The determinant argument is in characteristic zero; no strong reduction or general classification claim is made.
